Meanwhile, Heidi learnt that Grannie was blind and noticed how poorly
built their hut was. "I will ask Grandfather to fix the hut," she promised.
The next day, Heidi kept her promise
by bringing Grandfather to Grannie's hut
to fix things.
Heidi had spent a winter and a summer with Uncle Alp. When her second
winter on the mountain was about to end, a man in black visited them. It
was the pastor from Dorfli. Although surprised to see him, Uncle Alp greeted
him as politely as he could. "Morning, Pastor. Please have a seat." The pastor
refused the offer; instead, he told Uncle Alp straight away why he was there to
convince him to send Heidi to school.
Uncle Alp shook his head on the suggestion. "Heidi doesn't need to go to
school. She's fine here." He also expressed worries about the safety of Heidi's
travel to school and back in winter.
Later that day, a second visitor appeared to make the already angry
Grandfather even more so Detie was back and wanted to take Heidi to
Frankfurt to live in a family with a disabled girl. "It's a once-in-a-lifetime
opportunity! Heidi will become the girl's best friend, and they could play and
study together. Isn't that awesome?"
"Take her away and
never bring her back!" Then the old man stormed out of the hut.
Detie took Heidi to the Sesemanns,
a very wealthy family in Frankfurt. Mr.
Sesemann was often away working, so he
hired Miss Rottenmeier to look after his
wheelchair-bound daughter Clara. Since
the girl's mother died a long time ago,
Mr. Sesemann thought Clara's happiness
was his most important thing.
Miss Rottenmeier liked bossing servants around in the house. She was not
friendly. When she saw Heidi, she asked her about her name and age, but neither
of which satisfied her. "Heidi is not a proper name," and "You are not Clara's
age," were her words. When she learnt that Heidi couldn't read, she became very
surprised. "Good lord! What kind of girl your age doesn't read?" she said.
"Heidi, you may have some time to do what you please as Clara needs to
rest in the afternoon," said Miss Rottenmeier. Heidi was dying to see something
green. She chose to go out to climb up to the church tower bell as Sebastian
suggested. Since she was new to Frankfurt, she had to ask for directions from a
boy on her way. "You must pay me if I lead you there," the boy said.
"Fine," Heidi answered. "Go ask for money from Clara tomorrow."
Miss Rottenmeier into a panic as she was afraid of cats. "Get rid of those nasty
little cats, Sebastian!" she hurried out of the room while screaming the order.
"Sebastian, please, help us hide the kittens," pleaded Clara.
"Take it easy. No problems!"
